title: No screening address outlives its screening but as a keyed hash (audit #76; the founder's Q10 (a) and Q11 (b) of 2026-10-21)
assertion: The screening's SES set uses no suppression list, so SES keeps no screening address and no screening outcome silences a customer's mail; the mail record holds no address and no hash of one; the only values derived from a screening address kept past its prospect are the refusal list's keyed hash of the mailbox an address reaches (its every spelling: case, white space, a +tag, Gmail's dots, googlemail.com) that bounced permanently or was reported as spam on the screening stream, for 365 days, and the bounce budget's 7-day marks of the rate limiter's keyed subjects; the keyed hash differs from a plain SHA-256 of the address and changes with its pepper, which no role reads, and a scan of every text column after the mail scenarios finds it only on the refusal list; no address or domain appears in a log line, job payload, SES tag, audit event or error; no login role has a grant on the mail tables or may call the keyed hash; the application role may not write notice_undelivered, mail_stream_paused or mail_stream_resumed (42501)
noFileReason: The mail scenarios run on synthetic addresses at SES's simulator and on the migrated catalog, built in memory; no file.
